title: Rochester Heat Pump Rebates 2026: RG&E Amounts
desc: Rochester heat pump rebates 2026: RG&E pays up to $13,000 (Disadvantaged Community, Weatherized Tier, old system removed). What stacks and what ended.
lead: What Rochester homeowners can really get in 2026, checked against RG&E and NYSERDA on October 3, 2026.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Rochester in 2026
cards_intro:
Short answer: In Rochester, the main heat pump rebate is NYS Clean Heat (run by RG&E): up to $13,000 (Disadvantaged Community, Weatherized Tier, old system removed) for a whole-home system, taken off your contractor’s bill. It is one rebate, not several that add up. Lower-income households can get much more through EmPower+, and the federal tax credits ended on December 31, 2025.

Amounts for a single-family home. You get one line from this table, not several.
after_cards: NYSEG and RG&E share this table. Apartments and homes under 1,000 sq ft get about half. The Weatherized Tier (from September 1, 2026) applies to homes built after 2010, homes that took part in an approved weatherization program, or homes that pass a heating-load test. Your participating contractor applies for you.
sections:
Important: the City of Rochester is served by RG&E (Rochester Gas and Electric), not National Grid. RG&E runs NYS Clean Heat here, so the amounts in the table are RG&E’s. (This page sits in our National Grid section only for historical reasons.) A few outlying towns in Monroe County are on National Grid, so check the name on your electric bill.

Rochester has a large stock of early-1900s single-family homes with basements and forced-air or hot-water heat. Homes with ducts can often use a ducted heat pump, while radiator homes usually need ductless heads.

Lake-effect snow off Lake Ontario means the outdoor unit needs a stand above the snow line. RG&E, like the other upstate utilities, only pays Clean Heat for cold-climate listed equipment.

RG&E and NYSEG are sister utilities, so you may see their names together on program pages. The Rochester amounts are RG&E’s, which are slightly different from NYSEG’s in Disadvantaged Communities.

Clean Heat is the RG&E rebate, so never add the two together. Clean Heat is capped at 70% of cost (85% in a DAC). There is no separate federal HEAR cheque: New York delivers it through EmPower+. The federal 25C/25D tax credits ended December 31, 2025.

Income-qualified? EmPower+ can cover far more than the utility rebate. Check the state DAC map too: it can raise your amount.
claim_heading: What to do next in Rochester
claim_steps: Check the name on your bill: RG&E in the city, but some suburbs differ.
Ask for a snow stand for the outdoor unit in the quote.
Get 2–3 quotes and ask each contractor to show the rebate tier on the quote.
faq: How much is the heat pump rebate in Rochester?

NYS Clean Heat (run by RG&E) pays up to $13,000 (Disadvantaged Community, Weatherized Tier, old system removed) for a whole-home heat pump in Rochester, depending on home size, whether you remove the old system, and DAC status.
Is Rochester served by National Grid or RG&E?

The City of Rochester is served by RG&E (Rochester Gas and Electric). RG&E runs NYS Clean Heat here, paying up to $10,000 for a whole-home switch. A few outlying towns are on National Grid, so check your bill.
Is the federal tax credit still available for heat pumps?
No. The federal 25C and 25D credits ended for anything installed after December 31, 2025.

Lower-income owners and renters of 1-4 family homes. Low-income households can get free upgrades up to $12,000 upstate or $14,000 downstate; moderate-income households get 50% covered up to $6,000 upstate or $7,000 downstate.
